stocks.name: Apple
stocks.summary: Apple is up modestly today (+0.3%) and has rallied 8.8% over the month, sitting 2.2% below its 52‑week high and still 40.3% above its low. The stock remains near the top of its range, so investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance for signs of sustained momentum.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.summary: Microsoft slipped 1.4% on the day and is down 8.8% from its 52‑week peak, though still 39.2% above its low. With YTD growth modest at 4.3%, the next catalyst is the company’s cloud spending outlook in its upcoming earnings call.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.summary: Nvidia ticked higher 0.8% but remains 9.1% off its 52‑week high after a recent pullback of 4.8% this month. The key watch is whether AI demand can reignite growth, especially in the next earnings report.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.summary: Alphabet fell 0.6% today, trading 14.7% below its 52‑week high yet 45.3% above its low, with a flat month. Investors should focus on ad‑revenue trends and any updates to its AI product rollout.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.summary: Amazon is down 1.0% and sits 13.4% under its 52‑week high, having slipped 5.9% over the past month. The next driver will be retail sales trends and cloud growth guidance in the upcoming quarter.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.summary: Meta rose 0.5% and is 13.4% below its 52‑week high, after a strong 18.3% monthly gain. Watch user growth metrics and the rollout of its AI and metaverse initiatives for next‑move direction.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.summary: Tesla edged up 0.4% but remains 26.9% below its 52‑week high, with YTD performance down 18.3%. The upcoming production and pricing updates, especially for new models, will be critical to watch.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.summary: Broadcom inched up 0.1% but is 29.4% off its 52‑week high after a 13.5% monthly decline. Investors should monitor its semiconductor demand outlook and any guidance on margin pressure.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.summary: AMD jumped 1.6% and is only 11.8% below its 52‑week high, having surged 129.3% YTD and sitting 225.6% above its low. The next focus is the company’s product roadmap and competitive positioning in the GPU market.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.summary: Oracle has rallied 2.0% on the day but remains 55.9% below its 52‑week high, trading near the lower end of its range. The recent bounce follows a steep 11.4% weekly decline, suggesting short‑term volatility. Investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance and cloud‑software contract updates for direction.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.summary: Salesforce is up 2.0% today, sitting just 5.4% shy of its 52‑week peak after a strong 31.2% monthly gain. The stock remains well above its 52‑week low, reflecting a solid recovery from earlier weakness. Key focus will be the next quarterly results and progress on its AI‑driven product roadmap.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.summary: JPMorgan Chase slipped 1.0% intraday, trading 4.5% below its 52‑week high while still 24.6% above its low. The modest weekly decline follows an 8.7% YTD gain, indicating resilience amid rate‑sensitive earnings. Watch for Fed policy signals and the bank’s loan‑loss provisions in the upcoming earnings release.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.summary: Bank of America fell 2.7% on the day, now 10.2% under its 52‑week high but 25.2% above its low. The stock’s recent slide mirrors broader banking sector pressure from higher rates and credit concerns. Investors should monitor net interest margin trends and the bank’s credit‑quality metrics in the next report.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.summary: Visa dipped 1.2% but remains only 3.4% below its 52‑week high, holding near the top of its range after a modest 7.7% YTD rise. The slight weekly uptick suggests steady transaction volume despite mixed macro data. Next catalyst is the quarterly earnings beat and any updates on fee‑rate pressure from digital‑payment competition.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.summary: Mastercard is down 1.0% today, trading 5.4% below its 52‑week high and 20.6% above its low, with flat weekly performance. The modest YTD gain of 1.3% reflects cautious investor sentiment. Watch for the upcoming earnings call and guidance on cross‑border volume and pricing trends.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.summary: Netflix slipped 1.9% on the day, still 38.4% under its 52‑week high but 13.0% above its low after a modest 0.5% weekly rise. The stock’s 16% YTD decline highlights subscriber growth concerns. Key watch point is the next subscriber‑growth report and any pricing strategy changes.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.summary: Eli Lilly edged up 0.2% and sits 11.1% below its 52‑week high, comfortably above its low after a 5.8% YTD gain. The modest weekly rise follows a slight monthly dip, indicating stable demand for its pipeline. Investors should focus on upcoming FDA decisions and sales trends for its diabetes/obesity drugs.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.summary: UnitedHealth slipped 0.2% and remains 13.5% under its 52‑week high, still 46.6% above its low after a solid 13.8% YTD increase. The recent 4.6% monthly decline raises questions on enrollment growth. Watch the next earnings release for insight on medical‑cost trends and Medicare Advantage enrollment.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.summary: Johnson & Johnson is flat on the day, up 0.0%, and has risen 2.4% over the month, sitting 4.0% below its 52‑week high and still 56.9% above its 52‑week low. The stock’s modest YTD gain of 31.0% reflects steady earnings momentum. Investors should watch upcoming drug pipeline updates and any guidance on cost pressures.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.summary: Walmart slipped 0.5% today and is down 5.7% for the month, trading 19.7% below its 52‑week high but only 7.7% above its 52‑week low. The YTD decline of 4.1% signals pressure on margins amid competitive pricing. Key focus will be the latest same‑store sales trends and any shifts in its e‑commerce strategy.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.summary: Costco fell 0.8% on the day and is off 6.3% for the month, now 18.2% under its 52‑week high while 5.6% above its 52‑week low. A modest 5.1% YTD gain shows resilience, but the recent pullback raises questions on membership renewal rates. Watch the upcoming earnings for insight into inventory turnover and pricing power.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.summary: Home Depot dropped 1.0% today and is down 9.8% for the month, sitting 25.5% below its 52‑week high and just 3.2% above its 52‑week low. The 10.6% YTD decline reflects a broader housing slowdown. Investors should monitor housing market data and the company’s DIY versus professional segment performance.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.summary: Exxon Mobil slid 3.5% intraday, its biggest daily drop, and is 3.5% under its 52‑week high while still 51.9% above its 52‑week low. A 35.8% YTD rise underscores strong earnings from higher oil prices. The next catalyst is the upcoming quarterly results and any guidance on capital allocation amid volatile commodity prices.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.summary: Coca‑Cola slipped 0.9% today, down 1.6% for the month and trading 3.9% below its 52‑week high but 37.4% above its 52‑week low. The 29.6% YTD gain highlights solid demand despite price pressures. Watch the company’s pricing strategy and volume trends in its emerging‑market segment.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.summary: Disney rose 0.5% on the day and is up 3.4% for the month, still 7.0% below its 52‑week high while 16.7% above its 52‑week low. The modest YTD decline of 3.6% follows recent streaming and park challenges. Key focus will be the next earnings beat, especially the performance of Disney+ and theme‑park attendance.
